findings.message: This only fixes one case of the earlier blocker. Freezing the context stops callers changing it after issue. The main part of the finding is not fixed: `contextFor.job` is still exported from `@amax/core/server`, and every module, chat intent and MCP tool can import it. Any code can still call `contextFor.job(anyTenantId, "made-up")` and get a context that `isSystemContext` accepts. That context reads unmasked pay and bank data through getEmployment and passes `inScope` and `applyStatusDates`. The audit row then records a job name the caller invented. `modules/hr/server/jobs.ts:11` still mints its own context, and the diff adds no test showing that module code can't get an accepted system context. Fix: only the job runner (runDueJobs or the workflow engine) should mint system contexts, through a capability or factory that is not on the module import surface. The runner passes the context to the handler. Add a test showing that importing `@amax/core/server` from module code does not yield an accepted system context.
findings.scenario: An MCP tool or chat intent in any module calls `getEmployment(contextFor.job(tenantId, "x"), personId)` → salary, EPF and bank account come back unmasked, with an audit actor of `job:x`.

findings.message: The department scope for writes is taken from the employment in force today (`employmentAt(today())`). The write itself is applied at `effectiveOn`, and `newPeriod` also rewrites later periods. So the check looks at a different period from the one being changed. A department change is also not checked against the department it moves the person into. Fix: check scope against the department of every period the write touches (the period in force on `effectiveOn` and every later period it rewrites). When the input sets `department`, check the target department too.
findings.scenario: A person is in Finance today and has a planned transfer to Engineering on 2026-12-01. An HR user scoped to Finance calls `changePerson({ employeeNo, effectiveOn: "2027-01-01", grade: "E5" })` → `inScope` passes on Finance, and the HR user changes a period that belongs to Engineering.

findings.message: The new `inforce.ts` comment says reads, masking and writes 'all check this one subject'. But `inScope` takes its own subject shape `{ legalEntityId, department }` and passes on only those two fields. It drops `ownerUserId`, which `subjectOf` (and the read path) includes. Reads and writes can therefore still evaluate different subjects for an owner-narrowed assignment. Pass the full `subjectOf` result through to `assertCan`, or correct the comment.

The new department-scope test covers addPerson and changePerson but not recordLeaver, which also switched to `subjectOf(p)`. It also has no case where today's department differs from the department at `effectiveOn`. Add a recordLeaver row and a future-dated case.
